column1: # Words Telugu speakers routinely write in Telugu script but which are NOT
# phonetically derivable from the Telugu phonetic rules: English spelling says
# little about English sound, so "school" would come out స్చూల్ and "phone"
# ఫొనే. Typed on the Telugu phonetic layout, the English spelling on the left
# resolves directly to the Telugu form on the right, ahead of the rules and of
# A hand-written draft that wants a Telugu speaker's review. A wrong entry here
# is worse than a missing one, since it outranks everything. Where Telugu adds
# its own final -u (బస్సు, ఆఫీసు, డాక్టరు) both forms are listed, the commoner
# in the Telugu word list first. Compounds are written as plain conjuncts
# Format: english<TAB>telugu   (one mapping per line; # starts a comment)
# Keep the English key lowercase. First column is matched case-insensitively.
